Sortable data table with ARIA table semantics and keyed rows.

```ocaml
(* Sort types *)
type sort_direction = Ascending | Descending

type sort = {
  column : string;
  direction : sort_direction;
}

(* A column definition *)
type ('row, 'msg) column = {
  header : string;
  cell : 'row -> 'msg Element.t;
  sort_key : string option;
}

(* Configuration for rendering a data table *)
type ('row, 'msg) config = {
  columns : ('row, 'msg) column list;
  rows : 'row list;
  key : 'row -> string;
  sort : sort option;
  on_sort : string -> 'msg;
  style : Style.t option;
  header_style : Style.t option;
  row_style : Style.t option;
  cell_style : Style.t option;
  interaction : Interaction.t option;
  attrs : (string * string) list;
  column_style : (('row, 'msg) column -> Style.t option) option;
  sort_control_style : Style.t option;
  header_interaction : Interaction.t option;
  header_row_style : Style.t option;
}

(* Constructor — sort_key defaults to None *)
val column : header:string -> cell:('row -> 'msg Element.t)
  -> ?sort_key:string -> unit -> ('row, 'msg) column

(* Constructor — every optional field defaults to None/[], including the four
   override fields, which make does not take *)
val make : columns:('row, 'msg) column list -> rows:'row list
  -> key:('row -> string) -> on_sort:(string -> 'msg)
  -> ?sort:sort -> ?style:Style.t -> ?header_style:Style.t
  -> ?row_style:Style.t -> ?cell_style:Style.t
  -> ?interaction:Interaction.t
  -> ?attrs:(string * string) list -> unit -> ('row, 'msg) config

(* Per-column and header overrides — the supported route to the last four
   fields. *)
val with_column_style :
  (('row, 'msg) column -> Style.t option) -> ('row, 'msg) config
  -> ('row, 'msg) config
(* Styles one column at a time. f is asked for every column; Some s OUTRANKS
   header_style AND cell_style for that column, and reaches the column's HEADER
   CELL as well as its data cells, so a per-column width lines the column up
   with its own header. None leaves that column on the general styles. Keyed on
   the column VALUE because sort_key is optional — a non-sortable column has no
   name to key on; match on header or sort_key, since (=) on a column raises
   (cell is a function). *)

val with_sort_control_style :
  Style.t -> ('row, 'msg) config -> ('row, 'msg) config
(* Styles the button a column with a sort_key turns its header into.
   header_style and with_column_style land on the box AROUND that button, never
   on the button itself. *)

val with_header_interaction :
  Interaction.t -> ('row, 'msg) config -> ('row, 'msg) config
(* Hover/pressed/focused on every sortable header's button. Like
   with_sort_control_style it lands on the button, not on the header box. *)

val with_header_row_style :
  Style.t -> ('row, 'msg) config -> ('row, 'msg) config
(* Styles the header row itself — the role="row" element holding the header
   cells. row_style reaches only the data rows. *)

(* View *)
val view : ('row, 'msg) config -> 'msg Element.t
(* Renders a column container with role="table". Header row contains
   role="columnheader" cells — sortable columns wrap a button inside
   the columnheader box that dispatches on_sort with the column's
   sort_key. Active sort column carries aria-sort="ascending" or
   "descending". Data rows have role="row", cells have role="cell".
   Each data row is wrapped in Element.keyed using config.key. *)
```

Usage pattern — subapp integration:

```ocaml
(* Model *)
type model = { people : person list; sort : Data_table.sort option }

(* Messages *)
type msg = Sort of string

(* Update *)
let update model = function
  | Sort key ->
      let direction = match model.sort with
        | Some s when s.column = key && s.direction = Ascending -> Descending
        | _ -> Ascending
      in
      let sort = Some Data_table.{ column = key; direction } in
      let people = sort_by key direction model.people in
      ({ people; sort }, Cmd.none)

(* View *)
let view model =
  let config =
    Data_table.make
      ~columns:[
        Data_table.column ~header:"Name"
          ~cell:(fun p -> Element.text p.name)
          ~sort_key:"name" ();
        Data_table.column ~header:"Age"
          ~cell:(fun p -> Element.text (string_of_int p.age))
          ~sort_key:"age" ();
      ]
      ~rows:model.people
      ~key:(fun p -> p.name)
      ~on_sort:(fun key -> Sort key)
      ?sort:model.sort
      ()
  in
  Data_table.view config
```

#### Button

Button with variants (Primary, Secondary, Destructive, Ghost, Icon), loading
and disabled states.

```ocaml
(* Variants *)
type variant = Primary | Secondary | Destructive | Ghost | Icon

(* Configuration — all fields except variant have sensible defaults *)
type 'msg config = {
  variant : variant;
  disabled : bool;
  loading : bool;
  on_click : 'msg option;
  style : Style.t option;
  interaction : Interaction.t option;
  attrs : (string * string) list;
  disabled_style : Style.t option;
  loading_style : Style.t option;
  button_type : Element.button_type;
}
(* A complete record literal must now supply button_type (Push keeps the
   non-submitting default); the supported route is with_button_type. *)

val default : variant -> 'msg config
(* [default v] returns a config for variant [v] with disabled=false,
   loading=false, on_click=None, default style/interaction, empty attrs,
   no disabled or loading style, and button_type=Push: the button submits the
   form it sits in only when it is given Submit. *)

val with_button_type : Element.button_type -> 'msg config -> 'msg config
(* With Submit, activating the button inside an Element.form dispatches its
   on_click and then submits the form; with Push, its on_click alone. *)

val with_disabled_style : Style.t -> 'msg config -> 'msg config
(* The treatment while disabled. The component makes no visual distinction of
   its own — it renders aria-disabled, element-derived, and nothing else — so
   this INTRODUCES the decision, and with both setters unset the rendering is
   unchanged. It does not touch aria-disabled or the inert state. *)

val with_loading_style : Style.t -> 'msg config -> 'msg config
(* The treatment while loading. When both states hold, the DISABLED style
   outranks this one, and the two fall through: a loading style still applies
   to a disabled-and-loading button whose disabled style is unset. *)

val view : 'msg config -> 'msg Element.t -> 'msg Element.t
(* [view config child] renders a button element of type config.button_type.
   While disabled or loading the button is inert: a click dispatches nothing
   and submits nothing, and an Enter in a field of its form does not submit
   through it — when it is the form's first submit button, that Enter
   dispatches nothing at all, even if an enabled submit button follows it. It
   stays focusable and in the tab order, and a focused button keeps focus when
   it becomes inert. Both states carry aria-disabled="true"; loading also
   carries aria-busy="true".
   The style is disabled_style while disabled, else loading_style while
   loading, else config.style, else the variant default; interaction likewise
   falls back to the variant default.
   User attrs merged with ARIA attrs (user attrs take precedence), except
   "type" and "aria-disabled": those are derived from button_type and the
   inert state, so a caller's "type" pair never takes effect and a caller's
   "aria-disabled" pair only while the button is neither disabled nor
   loading. *)

val variant_to_string : variant -> string
(* Lowercase string name for test/debug. *)
```

#### Checkbox

Labelled checkbox component.

```ocaml
type 'msg config = {
  label : string;
  checked : bool;
  disabled : bool;
  on_toggle : (bool -> 'msg) option;
  style : Style.t option;
  interaction : Interaction.t option;
  attrs : (string * string) list;
  id : string option;
  label_style : Style.t option;
  row_style : Style.t option;
  on_label_click : 'msg option;
}

val make : label:string -> checked:bool -> 'msg config
(* [make ~label ~checked] returns a config with disabled=false,
   on_toggle=None, no style/interaction override, empty attrs, and no id,
   label style, row style or label-click message. *)

val with_id : string -> 'msg config -> 'msg config
(* The control's identifier, used verbatim. The supported route to it. Moves
   the control's id AND its aria-labelledby together; it does NOT move
   data-field, which stays on the slugified label because that anchor is an
   E2E selector contract. *)

val with_label_style : Style.t -> 'msg config -> 'msg config
(* The label box, and the label text's typography through that style's text
   component (handed over explicitly, never inherited). *)

val with_row_style : Style.t -> 'msg config -> 'msg config
(* The control-to-label Row — the gap between them. *)

val with_on_label_click : 'msg -> 'msg config -> 'msg config
(* Turns a pointer-down on the label into a message. Pair it with control_id
   and return Cmd.focus in update; a view function cannot issue a Cmd. *)

val control_id : 'msg config -> string
(* config.id when set, else the slugified label. The label element's own id is
   this value ^ "-label", which is what aria-labelledby points at. *)

val view : 'msg config -> 'msg Element.t
(* Renders a horizontal Row containing:
   1. An Element.checkbox carrying ("id", control_id config),
      ("aria-labelledby", control_id config ^ "-label") and
      ("data-field", slug(label))
   2. A label element — a Box carrying ("id", control_id config ^ "-label")
      and wrapping the label's text node
   The control is named by aria-labelledby and carries no aria-label of its
   own; an ("aria-label", _) pair pushed through config.attrs survives in the
   tree but does not name the control, because aria-labelledby wins the
   accessible-name computation. When disabled, on_toggle is suppressed. *)
```

#### Radio_group

Accessible radio button group component.

```ocaml
type radio_option = { label : string; value : string; disabled : bool }

type 'msg config = {
  label : string;
  options : radio_option list;
  selected : string;
  disabled : bool;
  name : string option;
  on_select : (string -> 'msg) option;
  style : Style.t option;      (* lands on each RADIO INPUT, not on the group *)
  interaction : Interaction.t option;  (* likewise per radio input *)
  attrs : (string * string) list;      (* lands on the group container *)
  id : string option;
  visible_label : bool option;
  label_style : Style.t option;
  group_style : Style.t option;
  option_label_style : Style.t option;
  option_row_style : Style.t option;
  on_label_click : (string -> 'msg) option;
}

val radio_option : ?disabled:bool -> value:string -> string -> radio_option
(* [radio_option ~value label] creates a radio option. disabled defaults to false. *)

val make : label:string -> options:radio_option list -> selected:string -> 'msg config
(* [make ~label ~options ~selected] returns a config with name=None
   (auto-generated from slugified label), disabled=false, on_select=None,
   no style/interaction override, empty attrs, and none of the seven
   override fields set. *)

val with_id : string -> 'msg config -> 'msg config
(* The group's identifier, used verbatim, and the stem every option id is
   derived from. Moves every id and every aria-labelledby together; it does NOT
   move data-field, which stays on the group name. *)

val with_visible_label : bool -> 'msg config -> 'msg config
(* Opts the group's own label ELEMENT in. OFF by default: the group renders no
   label text today, so making one appear is a rendered-tree change for every
   existing consumer. Until it is used the group keeps aria-label; with it the
   group's name moves to aria-labelledby pointing at the new element. *)

val with_label_style : Style.t -> 'msg config -> 'msg config
(* The group's own label box. INERT until with_visible_label true gives it an
   element to style. *)

val with_group_style : Style.t -> 'msg config -> 'msg config
(* The group container Column. Independent of config.style, which lands on each
   radio input instead. *)

val with_option_label_style : Style.t -> 'msg config -> 'msg config
(* Each option's label box, and its text typography through that style's text
   component. *)

val with_option_row_style : Style.t -> 'msg config -> 'msg config
(* Each option's radio-to-label Row. *)

val with_on_label_click : (string -> 'msg) -> 'msg config -> 'msg config
(* Turns a pointer-down on an OPTION's label into a message carrying that
   option's value — a group has many labels, so a single 'msg could not say
   which was pressed. The group's own label element carries no handler: it has
   no single control to act on. *)

val control_id : 'msg config -> string
(* config.id when set, else the slugified group label. On the group container
   unconditionally. *)

val option_id : 'msg config -> value:string -> string
(* control_id config ^ "-" ^ slugify value. Keyed on the VALUE, so two options
   sharing a value share an id. *)

val view : 'msg config -> 'msg Element.t
(* Renders a Column with role="radiogroup", ("id", control_id config), and
   aria-label=config.label — or aria-labelledby and a leading label element
   when with_visible_label true — containing one Row per option. Each Row has:
   1. An Element.radio (sharing the group name) carrying
      ("id", option_id config ~value),
      ("aria-labelledby", option_id config ~value ^ "-label") and
      ("data-field", <group name>)
   2. A label element — a Box carrying ("id", option_id … ^ "-label")
   Each option is named by aria-labelledby and carries no aria-label of its
   own. When config.disabled is true, all radios are disabled and on_select is
   suppressed. Per-option disabled is also respected. *)
```

#### Select_input

Labelled select dropdown component.

```ocaml
type 'msg config = {
  label : string;
  options : Element.select_option list;
  selected : string;
  placeholder : string option;
  disabled : bool;
  on_change : (string -> 'msg) option;
  style : Style.t option;
  interaction : Interaction.t option;
  attrs : (string * string) list;
  id : string option;
  label_style : Style.t option;
  wrapper_style : Style.t option;
  on_label_click : 'msg option;
}

val make : label:string -> options:Element.select_option list
  -> selected:string -> 'msg config
(* [make ~label ~options ~selected] returns a config with placeholder=None,
   disabled=false, on_change=None, no style/interaction override, empty attrs,
   and no id, label style, wrapper style or label-click message. *)

val with_id : string -> 'msg config -> 'msg config
(* The control's identifier, used verbatim. Moves the control's id AND its
   aria-labelledby together; it does NOT move data-field, which stays on the
   slugified label. *)

val with_label_style : Style.t -> 'msg config -> 'msg config
(* The label box, and the label text's typography through that style's text
   component. *)

val with_wrapper_style : Style.t -> 'msg config -> 'msg config
(* The label-to-control Column — the gap between them. *)

val with_on_label_click : 'msg -> 'msg config -> 'msg config
(* Pointer-down on the label as a message. Pair with control_id + Cmd.focus. *)

val control_id : 'msg config -> string
(* config.id when set, else the slugified label. *)

val view : 'msg config -> 'msg Element.t
(* Renders a vertical Column containing:
   1. A label element — a Box carrying ("id", control_id config ^ "-label")
      and wrapping the label's text node
   2. An Element.select carrying ("id", control_id config),
      ("aria-labelledby", control_id config ^ "-label"),
      ("data-action", "select-open") and ("data-field", slug(label))
   The control is named by aria-labelledby and carries no aria-label of its
   own. When placeholder is Some text, a disabled option with value="" is
   prepended. When disabled, on_change is suppressed. *)
```

#### Slug

URL-safe slug generation from human-readable strings.

```ocaml
val slugify : string -> string
(* [slugify s] lowercases [s], replaces whitespace and non-alphanumeric
   characters with hyphens, collapses consecutive hyphens, and trims
   leading/trailing hyphens. *)

val derive_id :
  explicit:string option -> label:string -> ?suffix:string -> unit -> string
(* The id-derivation convention every labelled control uses: [explicit] when the
   caller set one, else [slugify label]; [suffix] is appended after one hyphen,
   so ~suffix:"error" on "First Name" yields "first-name-error".
   [explicit] is used VERBATIM — never slugified — and wins even when it is the
   empty string. An empty label slugifies to "", so with no explicit id the
   answer is "" or "-error". Total; never raises; invents no non-empty
   fallback. *)
```

`Slug` renders nothing, so it makes no visual decision and has no override
surface.

#### Text_node

The label and error text node every override that carries typography goes
through: the four labelled controls' label and error text, `Navigation_bar`'s
item label, `Bottom_tabs`' back-affordance label. Shared helper, not a
component: its style is its argument, so it makes no visual decision of its own
and has no row in the audit table above.

```ocaml
val of_style : style:Style.t option -> string -> 'msg Element.t
(* [of_style ~style text] is the text node for [text]. With None it is
   Element.text — a node with no text style at all, byte for byte what a control
   with no style override has always rendered. With Some s it is
   Element.styled_text carrying s.text.
   Which arm applies is decided by the OPTION alone and never by the contents of
   s.text: Some with an all-None text component still produces a styled text
   node, so adding a style override never leaves the node looking unstyled.
   It exists because the label is a BOX carrying the generated id (styled_text
   takes no attrs) and nopal_test has no inheritance — a text node styled only
   by its parent reads as unstyled structurally while rendering correctly in a
   browser. That hand-off is written in exactly one place. *)
```

#### Text_input

Accessible text input with label and optional error message linked via aria-describedby.

```ocaml
type 'msg config = {
  label : string;
  value : string;
  placeholder : string option;
  error : string option;
  disabled : bool;
  id : string option;
  on_change : (string -> 'msg) option;
  on_submit : 'msg option;
  on_blur : 'msg option;
  style : Style.t option;
  interaction : Interaction.t option;
  attrs : (string * string) list;
  label_style : Style.t option;
  wrapper_style : Style.t option;
  error_style : Style.t option;
  on_label_click : 'msg option;
}

val make : label:string -> value:string -> 'msg config
(* [make ~label ~value] returns a config with all optional fields None,
   disabled=false, attrs=[]. *)

val with_id : string -> 'msg config -> 'msg config
(* Sets config.id: the input's id, and the stem the label's "-label" and the
   error slot's "-error" ids derive from. data-field moves with it — on THIS
   control alone, because it has always carried control_id. *)

val with_label_style : Style.t -> 'msg config -> 'msg config
(* The label box, and the label text's typography through that style's text
   component — the label WEIGHT and, with with_wrapper_style, the label-to-box
   gap, which are the two decisions a consumer once had to fork for. *)

val with_wrapper_style : Style.t -> 'msg config -> 'msg config
(* The outer Column holding label, input and error slot — its gap is the
   label-to-box distance. *)

val with_error_style : Style.t -> 'msg config -> 'msg config
(* The error slot box, and the error message's typography through that style's
   text component. *)

val with_on_label_click : 'msg -> 'msg config -> 'msg config
(* Pointer-down on the label as a message. Pair with control_id + Cmd.focus. *)

val control_id : 'msg config -> string
(* config.id when set, else the slugified label. This is the input's id, the
   value data-field carries, and the stem of the label and error ids. *)

val error_id : 'msg config -> string
(* Returns the identifier used for aria-describedby linkage. If config.id
   is Some id, returns id ^ "-error". Otherwise derives from slugified label. *)

val view : 'msg config -> 'msg Element.t
(* Renders a vertical column containing:
   1. A label element — a Box carrying ("id", control_id config ^ "-label")
      and wrapping the label's text node
   2. An input (Element.input) with value, placeholder and event handlers,
      carrying ("id", control_id config),
      ("aria-labelledby", control_id config ^ "-label") and
      ("data-field", control_id config)
   3. When config.error is Some msg, an error box with role="alert" and
      id=error_id; the input gains aria-describedby=error_id
   The input is named by aria-labelledby and carries no aria-label of its own;
   an ("aria-label", _) pair pushed through config.attrs survives in the tree
   but does not name the input. Pushing ("id", _) through config.attrs replaces
   the input's id at the attrs tier and the caller then owns re-pointing
   aria-labelledby; with_id (equivalently config.id) is the supported route.
   When disabled, input carries disabled="" and event handlers are suppressed. *)
```

**Component output that moved — read this on a pin bump.** Four components now
own the element that renders their label, so a control is named by
`aria-labelledby` pointing at that element instead of by its own `aria-label`.
Every existing function signature is unchanged, so a downstream structural suite
meets this with no compiler help — this list is the only warning it gets. The one
compile-visible change is the complete-literal break in the last table below. The "before" column is the
tree at commit `2198a3c`. Attribute rows and tree rows are kept apart: a node
appearing is not a key changing its answer, and a suite that asserts on shape
meets it differently. Both halves are pinned in both directions by
`test/unit/nopal_ui/test_change_list.ml`.

**Attribute rows — keys whose answer moved.**

| # | Node | Key | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `Text_input`'s input | `aria-label` | the label string | **absent** |
| 2 | `Text_input`'s input | `aria-labelledby` | absent | `control_id config ^ "-label"` |
| 3 | `Text_input`'s input | `id` | absent | `control_id config` |
| 4 | `Checkbox`'s checkbox | `aria-label` | the label string | **absent** |
| 5 | `Checkbox`'s checkbox | `aria-labelledby` | absent | `control_id config ^ "-label"` |
| 6 | `Checkbox`'s checkbox | `id` | absent | `control_id config` |
| 7 | `Select_input`'s select | `aria-label` | the label string | **absent** |
| 8 | `Select_input`'s select | `aria-labelledby` | absent | `control_id config ^ "-label"` |
| 9 | `Select_input`'s select | `id` | absent | `control_id config` |
| 10 | each `Radio_group` option's radio | `aria-label` | that option's label string | **absent** |
| 11 | each `Radio_group` option's radio | `aria-labelledby` | absent | `option_id config ~value ^ "-label"` |
| 12 | each `Radio_group` option's radio | `id` | absent | `option_id config ~value` |
| 13 | the `Radio_group` container | `id` | absent | `control_id config` |
| 14 | the `Radio_group` container, under `with_visible_label true` | `aria-label` | the group label string | **absent** |
| 15 | the `Radio_group` container, under `with_visible_label true` | `aria-labelledby` | absent | `control_id config ^ "-label"` |

Row 13 is unconditional, unlike the group's label element: `control_id` is
published, and an accessor whose value appears nowhere in the rendered tree would
be a published lie. Rows 14 and 15 apply only when the group label is opted in —
without the setter the group keeps `aria-label`, which is why it is not row 4's
shape.

Keys that did **not** move, recorded so a reader does not go looking:

- Every `data-*` anchor. `Text_input`'s `data-field` is `control_id` and always
  was. `Checkbox`'s and `Select_input`'s stay the **slugified label** and
  `with_id` deliberately does not move them; `Radio_group`'s stays the group
  `name`. The divergence from `Text_input` is deliberate — moving an anchor moves
  an E2E selector contract. `Select_input` also keeps `data-action="select-open"`.
- `Text_input`'s error slot keeps its `id` and `role="alert"`, and the input
  keeps `aria-describedby` when an error is present.
- The `Radio_group` container keeps `role="radiogroup"`, and keeps `aria-label`
  whenever the group label is not opted in.
- **No attribute moved on `Toast`, `Button`, `Data_table`, `Modal`,
  `Navigation_bar` or `Bottom_tabs`.** Every key those six emit answers exactly
  as it did, under every override old and new — including `Toast`'s own
  `aria-label`, which is a dismiss hint on the toast button and not a control's
  accessible name. Each of the six is pinned exhaustively by its own
  every-override-at-once case; `test_change_list.ml` reads a representative key
  per component so that the "nothing else moved" half of this list is pinned too.

**Tree rows — nodes that appear or change shape.** Five, and the last is opt-in.

| # | Container | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `Text_input`'s column | `[text; input]` | `[box; input]` |
| 2 | `Checkbox`'s row | `[checkbox; text]` | `[checkbox; box]` |
| 3 | `Select_input`'s column | `[text; select]` | `[box; select]` |
| 4 | each `Radio_group` option's row | `[radio; text]` | `[radio; box]` |
| 5 | the `Radio_group` container, under `with_visible_label true` | `[row; row]` | `[box; row; row]` |

Each new box carries `("id", <the label id>)` and wraps the label's text node, so
rows 1–4 add exactly one node per control and reorder nothing — the control is
still its container's first or second child, as it was. Row 5 puts the group's own
label element ahead of every option row; without the setter, and with `false`, no
such node exists. `Element.styled_text` and `Element.text` are the same node in
the structural tree — both are `Text { content; text_style }` — so a label whose
style setter is unset renders exactly the text node it always did, and no other
container in `nopal_ui` gains, loses or reorders a child.

**Compile-break rows.** Every override's state lives in a new `option` field
appended to the component's published `config` record, and every existing
`make`/`default` signature is unchanged and fills the new fields with `None`. A
consumer building a config with the constructor, or with `{ constructor … with … }`,
compiles untouched. A consumer writing a **complete record literal** does not: the
compiler says `Error: Some record fields are undefined: …` and the fix is to add
the listed fields as `None`.

| Config | New fields |
|---|---|
| `'msg Text_input.config` | `label_style`, `wrapper_style`, `error_style`, `on_label_click` |
| `'msg Checkbox.config` | `id`, `label_style`, `row_style`, `on_label_click` |
| `'msg Select_input.config` | `id`, `label_style`, `wrapper_style`, `on_label_click` |
| `'msg Radio_group.config` | `id`, `visible_label`, `label_style`, `group_style`, `option_label_style`, `option_row_style`, `on_label_click` |
| `'msg Toast.config` | `toast_style`, `toast_interaction` |
| `'msg Button.config` | `disabled_style`, `loading_style` |
| `('row, 'msg) Data_table.config` | `column_style`, `sort_control_style`, `header_interaction`, `header_row_style` |

`Modal.config`, `Navigation_bar.config` and `Bottom_tabs.config` are **abstract**
in their `.mli`s, so their new fields (`root_style`; `item_text_style`,
`item_row_style`, `item_interaction`; `back_style`, `tab_text_style`,
`tab_row_style`, `tab_interaction`) are invisible to every consumer and break nothing.

**Three cases named rather than left to be derived.**

1. **A consumer who overrode the accessible name through `~attrs`.** An
   `("aria-label", _)` pair pushed through `config.attrs` still survives in the
   tree and still wins its own key — that is the second tier of the
   attribute-precedence rule working as designed. But the control now also
   carries the component's `aria-labelledby`, and `aria-labelledby` wins the
   accessible-name computation, so that override is silently overridden. The
   replacement route, stated on all four `.mli`s: point `aria-labelledby` at your
   own element, or change the label text. `aria-label` no longer names these four
   controls. One caveat is on `Radio_group`: `config.attrs` reaches the group
   container only and never an option, so an option's name is a change to what
   the component contributes rather than something a call site can undo per
   option.
2. **`Radio_group`'s group label** is a rendered-tree change and not an attribute
   change, and it is **opt-in**: the group renders no label text today, so making
   one appear would be a tree change for every existing consumer, including those
   who built their own heading around its absence. `with_visible_label true` is
   what adds it, and only then does the group's name move to `aria-labelledby`.
3. **These ids must be unique on the page, and nothing enforces it.** Each is
   derived from the slugified label alone (`<base>`, `<base>-label`,
   `<base>-error`, and on `Radio_group` `<base>-<slug value>`), so two controls
   sharing a label emit the same `id` and both `aria-labelledby` associations
   resolve to the first label element; within one `Radio_group`, an option whose
   `value` slugifies to `label` collides with the group's own label element under
   `with_visible_label true`. Before this change none of these controls emitted an
   `id` at all, so the precondition is new. No uniqueness is invented for them —
   the caller settles it with `with_id`, and each `control_id` docblock says so.

**Two further changes travel with the rows above and move no key's answer.**

1. **A node's `attrs` list.** The four controls' control nodes gain pairs, and on
   `Text_input` the position of `data-field` inside that list shifts (the two
   naming pairs are contributed ahead of it). Every lookup answers as the table
   above says, but `Test_renderer.node` exposes `attrs` publicly, so a whole-list
   equality on one of those nodes sees a different list.
2. **No accessor was renamed or removed.** `Text_input.error_id` answers exactly
   as before. `control_id` on the four, and `Radio_group.option_id`, are new
   surface rather than renamed surface, so nothing downstream is spelled
   differently.

### Navigation Stack (`nopal_navigation`)

Pure stack-based navigation state for per-screen drill-down (e.g. one stack per
bottom tab). The type is non-empty by construction — a current screen always
exists — and `pop` is total: popping a stack holding only its root is a no-op,
never an error and never an absent value. No platform deps; compiles native.

```ocaml
type 'screen Nav_stack.t   (* abstract; non-empty *)

Nav_stack.create  : 'screen -> 'screen t       (* root only; can_pop = false *)
Nav_stack.push    : 'screen -> 'screen t -> 'screen t   (* new screen becomes current *)
Nav_stack.pop     : 'screen t -> 'screen t     (* total — no-op at root *)
Nav_stack.current : 'screen t -> 'screen       (* total — always defined *)
Nav_stack.depth   : 'screen t -> int           (* always >= 1 *)
Nav_stack.can_pop : 'screen t -> bool          (* depth > 1; check before offering "back" *)
Nav_stack.screens : 'screen t -> 'screen list  (* root first, current last; non-empty *)
```

### Routing (`nopal_platform`)

Type-safe bidirectional routing. `Router.create` consumes `(module Platform.NAV)` — routing needs only the navigation capability, so routing-only call sites are not forced to carry storage:

```ocaml
Router.create : platform:(module Platform.NAV) -> parse:(string -> 'route option)
  -> to_path:('route -> string) -> not_found:'route -> 'route Router.t

Router.current  : 'route Router.t -> 'route                    (* read current *)
Router.push     : 'route Router.t -> 'route -> 'msg Cmd.t      (* push history *)
Router.replace  : 'route Router.t -> 'route -> 'msg Cmd.t      (* replace current *)
Router.back     : 'route Router.t -> 'msg Cmd.t                (* go back *)
Router.on_navigate : 'route Router.t -> ('route -> 'msg) -> 'msg Sub.t  (* subscribe *)
```

### Platform Capabilities (`nopal_platform`)

`Platform` declares the capability signatures a backend must satisfy. `NAV` is the
navigation capability (consumed by `Router`); `S` bundles `NAV` with the storage
capability. Backends (`Platform_web`, `Platform_tauri`) ascribe `Platform.S`.

```ocaml
module Platform : sig
  module type NAV = sig
    val current_path  : unit -> string
    val push_state    : string -> unit
    val replace_state : string -> unit
    val back          : unit -> unit
    val on_popstate   : (string -> unit) -> unit -> unit
  end

  module type S = sig
    include NAV
    val storage : (module Nopal_storage.S)   (* the linked platform's storage backend *)
  end
end
```

### Offline Storage (`nopal_storage`)

Backend-agnostic, asynchronous key-value storage. Application code targets the
abstract `module type S` unchanged on every platform; the concrete backend is
supplied at the entry point via `Nopal_platform.Platform.S.storage`. Operations
return `Nopal_mvu.Task.t` — lift them into commands with `Cmd.task` from `update`.
`S` is a pure `string`-to-`string` interface (encryption/compression are wrapper
concerns, never backend concerns). No platform dependencies.

```ocaml
type Nopal_storage.error =
  | Quota_exceeded      of string
  | Permission_denied   of string
  | Backend_unavailable of string
  | Backend_error       of string   (* catch-all; carries the raw backend message *)

val Nopal_storage.message : error -> string   (* human-readable, for display *)

module type Nopal_storage.S = sig
  val get    : string -> (string option, error) result Nopal_mvu.Task.t
    (* Ok (Some v) when present, Ok None when absent *)
  val set    : key:string -> value:string -> (unit, error) result Nopal_mvu.Task.t
    (* labelled: both args are string *)
  val delete : string -> (unit, error) result Nopal_mvu.Task.t
    (* deleting an absent key resolves Ok () *)
  val keys   : ?prefix:string -> unit -> (string list, error) result Nopal_mvu.Task.t
    (* order unspecified; ?prefix restricts to matching keys *)
  val clear  : unit -> (unit, error) result Nopal_mvu.Task.t
    (* clears this abstraction's namespace only — never localStorage / Nopal_tauri.Store *)
end

(* Generative in-memory backend; isolated per application, resolves synchronously.
   Native-clean — ideal for tests. *)
module Nopal_storage.In_memory () : sig
  include Nopal_storage.S
  val reset : unit -> unit   (* empties the store, for test isolation *)
end

(* Typed encode/decode wrapper over any Nopal_storage.S backend. *)
module Nopal_storage.With_codec (Store : Nopal_storage.S) : sig
  type typed_error = Storage of error | Decode of string
  val get : string -> decode:(string -> ('a, string) result)
            -> ('a option, typed_error) result Nopal_mvu.Task.t
  val set : key:string -> value:'a -> encode:('a -> string)
            -> (unit, error) result Nopal_mvu.Task.t
end
```

Concrete backends (each `module Make () : Nopal_storage.S`, selected by which
platform module is linked):

```ocaml
module Nopal_storage_web.Make   () : Nopal_storage.S
  (* IndexedDB (database nopal_storage, object store kv). Survives reloads; no ~5 MB cap. *)
module Nopal_storage_tauri.Make () : Nopal_storage.S
  (* One file per key under a scoped app-data subdirectory via tauri-plugin-fs. Survives relaunch. *)
```

Application usage (native-clean functor pattern; the concrete platform appears
only in `main.ml`):

```ocaml
(* app.ml — platform-agnostic *)
module Make (Platform : Nopal_platform.Platform.S) = struct
  module Storage = (val Platform.storage)
  (* update: Cmd.task (Task.map to_msg (Storage.get key)) *)
end

(* main.ml *)
module App = App.Make (Platform_web)
```

### Image (`nopal_image`)

Pure pixel data: a validated RGBA buffer, its conversion to perceptual luminance,
a sharpness (focus) metric over that luminance, the capture parameters a platform
backend reads, and the three seams a platform backend registers itself into —
`Processing` for turning a stored image into an upload-ready one, `Preview` for
getting a stored image on screen, `Retention` for releasing one it is finished with.
The only dependency is `nopal_mvu`, which supplies the `Task.t` and `Cmd.t` types
the seams state their effect in; the package still compiles native, so the metric is
testable without a browser. Nothing here touches compressed bytes, a canvas, or
any platform API: encoding, resizing and EXIF are the platform backend's concern,
and `nopal_image` only describes them — a canvas is named in a `Processing`
failure but never reached for.

```ocaml
type Nopal_image.error =
  | Invalid_dimensions of string   (* w, h and byte length cannot describe an image *)
  | Invalid_config     of string   (* a capture parameter outside its permitted range *)

val Nopal_image.message : error -> string   (* human-readable, for display *)

module Nopal_image.Image_error   (* same type, re-exported so the submodule
                                    signatures naming it read without an
                                    internal module path *)
```

`Buffer.t` is abstract and validated at construction — both dimensions positive,
exactly four bytes per pixel — so every later read is safe index arithmetic.
`create` copies the incoming `bytes`, so the caller may reuse or mutate its own
source afterwards without affecting the buffer. There is no accessor returning
the raw bytes. Every module below is reached through the entry module
(`Nopal_image.Buffer`, `Nopal_image.Luma`, …); note that `open Nopal_image`
shadows `Stdlib.Buffer`, so qualify the stdlib module if you need it.

```ocaml
type Nopal_image.Buffer.t   (* abstract; immutable; validated *)

Buffer.create : width:int -> height:int -> rgba:bytes
                -> (Buffer.t, Nopal_image.error) result
                (* Error (Invalid_dimensions _) on a non-positive edge or a
                   byte length inconsistent with the dimensions *)
Buffer.width     : Buffer.t -> int          (* always positive *)
Buffer.height    : Buffer.t -> int          (* always positive *)
Buffer.byte_size : Buffer.t -> int          (* packed RGBA size in bytes *)
Buffer.pixel     : Buffer.t -> x:int -> y:int -> (int * int * int * int) option
                (* r, g, b, a each 0-255; None out of range (total, never raises).
                   Zero-based, origin at the top left. *)
```

Luminance uses the standard perceptual weights (0.299 R, 0.587 G, 0.114 B) — the
same ones JPEG encodes with — not a channel average, which would give blue about
five times the weight the eye gives it. Channels and result are both on the 0-255
scale, so a gray pixel maps to its own value. Alpha takes no part.

```ocaml
Luma.of_channels : r:int -> g:int -> b:int -> float   (* 0-255 in, 0-255 out *)
Luma.of_buffer   : Buffer.t -> float array
                 (* one entry per pixel, row-major: left to right, then top to bottom *)
```

`Sharpness.score` is the mean absolute luminance difference over every
horizontally AND vertically adjacent pair, on the same 0-255 scale; higher is
sharper. Summing both axes makes it orientation-independent (a quarter turn
leaves the score unchanged bar the last bits of floating-point summation);
dividing by the pair count removes the dependence on how many pixels there are,
which a raw sum would carry. It is total — a single-pixel buffer has no adjacent
pair and scores `0.0`, never NaN. Two caveats. It measures contrast, so the same
subject at the same focus scores lower in dim light. And the normalization does
NOT make scores comparable across *resampling*: downscaling changes the pixel
values themselves, not just the pair count, so compare only scores measured at
the same edge (i.e. at one fixed `Config.metric_edge`). There is no built-in
pass/fail threshold and none is offered — choosing one is the consuming
application's own calibration.

```ocaml
Sharpness.score : Buffer.t -> float   (* total; 0.0 for a 1x1 buffer *)
```

`Config.t` is abstract with an all-required `make` and one named preset — there is
no `default` record and no field-wise update path, so a custom set states all four
values. `format` is a nominal variant, never a MIME string at the API boundary;
`format_to_mime` is for a platform encoder that takes its target as a string.

```ocaml
type Nopal_image.Config.format = Jpeg | Png | Webp
type Nopal_image.Config.t   (* abstract; validated *)

Config.make : max_edge:int -> metric_edge:int -> quality:float -> format:format
              -> (Config.t, Nopal_image.error) result
              (* Error (Invalid_config _) on a non-positive edge,
                 metric_edge > max_edge, or quality outside 0.0-1.0 (NaN rejected) *)
Config.recommended : Config.t       (* 1600 / 800 / 0.8 / Jpeg *)
Config.max_edge    : Config.t -> int    (* long edge the stored image scales down to *)
Config.metric_edge : Config.t -> int    (* long edge the sharpness pass scales down to *)
Config.quality     : Config.t -> float  (* 0.0-1.0, as the caller supplied it *)
Config.format      : Config.t -> format
Config.format_to_mime : format -> string   (* "image/jpeg" | "image/png" | "image/webp" *)
```

`Processing` is the platform-free seam an application calls to have a stored image
turned into an upload-ready one. It is shaped exactly like `Nopal_http`'s backend
seam: a record of functions, a `default_backend` that fails rather than hangs, a
`register_backend` called once at mount, and a `Cmd`-returning entry point. An App
module can name every type here without importing any platform package;
`nopal_image_web` supplies the browser implementation.

```ocaml
type Nopal_image.Processing.error =
  | Blob_not_found     of string   (* no stored image under the handle asked for *)
  | Decode_failed      of string   (* the stored bytes did not decode as an image *)
  | Canvas_unavailable of string   (* the drawing surface could not be obtained *)
  | Pixel_read_failed  of string   (* the drawn pixels could not be read back *)
  | Encode_failed      of string   (* the processed pixels did not re-encode *)

Processing.message : error -> string
      (* "Image decode failed: <detail>" and the four siblings — for display.
         The detail is a sentence for a human, never a token to branch on. *)

type Nopal_image.Processing.result_info = {
  blob_id   : string;   (* NEW handle from the blob store; the processed handle
                           keeps its own entry and stays usable *)
  width     : int;      (* size the processed image was ACTUALLY stored at,
                           read back off the canvas — not echoed from the config *)
  height    : int;
  byte_size : int;      (* length of the ENCODED blob. A different quantity from
                           Buffer.byte_size, which is the raw RGBA length for the
                           same picture, larger by roughly an order of magnitude *)
  sharpness : float;    (* Sharpness.score over a second, smaller draw of the
                           SAME image, scaled to Config.metric_edge BEFORE any
                           encoding — NOT over what was encoded and stored. A
                           rejection threshold calibrated against it moves with
                           metric_edge, never with quality *)
}

type Nopal_image.Processing.backend = {
  process : blob_id:string -> config:Config.t
            -> (result_info, error) result Nopal_mvu.Task.t;
}

Processing.default_backend  : backend
      (* in force before any platform registers one; resolves
         Error (Canvas_unavailable _) — never raises, never leaves the task
         unresolved. Public so a test can restore it. *)
Processing.register_backend : backend -> unit
Processing.process : blob_id:string -> config:Config.t
                     -> ((result_info, error) result -> 'msg) -> 'msg Nopal_mvu.Cmd.t

(* main.ml, once, before any command is built:
     Nopal_image.Processing.register_backend
       { Nopal_image.Processing.process = Nopal_image_web.process }

   process reads the registered backend when the COMMAND IS BUILT, not when the
   task runs — same as Nopal_http.send. Build it inside update; a command built at
   module initialisation captures default_backend, because main.ml has not
   registered yet. *)
```

`Preview` is the second seam in the same shape: `Processing` turns a stored
image into an upload-ready one, `Preview` gets a stored image on screen. It
hands back a platform reference naming bytes the blob store already holds — a
browser object URL, under the web backend — so an application can show a picture
it has stored without reading those bytes back into OCaml. `Element.image` takes
a `src` string, so nothing in `nopal_element` had to change for this.

The lifetime is the thing to get right. A minted URL PINS its image until it is
released, releasing is only ever something the application asks for (no runtime,
unmount or collector does it), and every mint is a separate resource — two mints
are two releases. An application that replaces one displayed picture with
another releases the URL it is replacing FIRST, or every picture it has ever
shown stays resident for the page session. The kitchen sink's receipt section is
the worked example of that hygiene, including the case where a URL arrives after
the request for it was superseded and has to be released on arrival.

```ocaml
type Nopal_image.Preview.error =
  | Blob_not_found      of string   (* no stored image under the handle asked for *)
  | Url_unavailable     of string   (* stored, but this platform minted no URL for it *)
  | Backend_unregistered of string  (* nothing was registered — a wiring failure in
                                       the application, not a property of the image *)

Preview.message : error -> string   (* human-readable, for display *)

type Nopal_image.Preview.backend = {
  url    : blob_id:string -> (string, error) result Nopal_mvu.Task.t;
  revoke : url:string -> unit;   (* cannot fail: a URL already released, or one
                                    this backend never minted, is a no-op *)
}

Preview.default_backend  : backend
      (* in force before any platform registers one; its url resolves
         Error (Backend_unregistered _) rather than raising or hanging, and its
         revoke does nothing. Public so a test can restore it. *)
Preview.register_backend : backend -> unit
Preview.preview_url : blob_id:string
                      -> ((string, error) result -> 'msg) -> 'msg Nopal_mvu.Cmd.t
Preview.revoke      : url:string -> 'msg Nopal_mvu.Cmd.t

(* revoke is a Cmd.perform and dispatches NO message: releasing cannot fail, so
   there is no outcome to report and no reply to wait for. Both builders read the
   registered backend when the COMMAND IS BUILT, exactly as Processing.process
   and Nopal_http.send do — build them inside update.

   Four seams are now built in this shape (nopal_http, Processing, Preview,
   Retention). This note used to name the fourth consumer as the trigger for lifting
   a shared registry. The fourth arrived, the lift was evaluated against it, and
   it was DECLINED. What repeats across the four is not a near-identical block:
   the four backend records share nothing but the name — { process },
   { url; revoke }, { release } and { send } have no field, no arity and no
   result type in common — so what the four sites hold identically is a ref and
   a one-line setter read at four unrelated types, two lines whose only
   differing content is the type they stand at. The shape has DIVERGED exactly
   where a lift would have to bind it, and that is the ground. Two lesser ones:
   the eight lines across the four have no shared home (three in nopal_image,
   nopal_http in its own package), so a shared registry needs a fifth package or
   a widening of nopal_mvu's remit; and each register_backend is documented with
   prose about its own seam, which a shared one cannot carry — visible only on
   the attempt to write the fourth.

   No further count re-opens this. What would: a seam whose registration needs
   behaviour rather than storage, or a third package acquiring one of these
   seams. The cross-package split is NOT a ground on its own — it already
   existed when the count was three, so the trigger was set without weighing
   it. *)
```

`Retention` is this package's third seam in that shape, and the one that ends a
stored image's life. A stored image is bytes the platform holds under a handle and it
stays held until something releases it — no runtime, unmount or collector does
it — so an application that keeps storing pictures and never releases the ones
it has stopped using retains every one of them for the session. Releasing an
entry is NOT revoking a URL minted from it: `Preview.revoke` frees the URL and
leaves the entry registered and still able to mint again, `Retention.release` frees
the entry, and neither performs the other. An application finished with a
picture it was displaying asks for BOTH.

```ocaml
type Nopal_image.Retention.backend = {
  release : blob_id:string -> unit;   (* cannot fail: a handle this backend
                                         never issued, or one it has already
                                         released, is a no-op *)
}

Retention.default_backend  : backend
      (* in force before any platform registers one; releases nothing, because
         nothing can have been stored through a platform that never registered
         itself. Inert rather than raising — release reports no outcome, so a
         raise would abandon the caller with nothing to respond to. Public so a
         test can restore it. *)
Retention.register_backend : backend -> unit
Retention.release : blob_id:string -> 'msg Nopal_mvu.Cmd.t

(* release is a Cmd.perform and dispatches NO message: releasing cannot fail, so
   there is no outcome to report and no reply to wait for, and 'msg stays free
   because no message is ever made. It has no error type and no result — this is
   deliberate, not an omission, and a caller may release whatever it happens to
   hold without keeping a record of what it has already released.

   The backend is read when the COMMAND IS BUILT, as in the two seams above.
   Build it inside update. *)
```

### Scene Types (`nopal_scene`)

Pure scene description types used by `Element.draw` and `nopal_draw`. No platform dependencies.
`nopal_element` depends on `nopal_scene` (not `nopal_draw`), keeping the element DSL free of drawing algorithms.

```ocaml
(* Re-exports: Color, Paint, Transform, Path (segment types + builders), Scene *)
(* These are also available via Nopal_draw.Color, Nopal_draw.Scene, etc. *)
```

### 2D Drawing (`nopal_draw`)

Higher-level drawing utilities built on `nopal_scene`. Re-exports all `nopal_scene` modules for convenience:

```ocaml
(* Colors — float 0.0-1.0 range *)
Color.rgba : r:float -> g:float -> b:float -> a:float -> Color.t
Color.rgb  : r:float -> g:float -> b:float -> Color.t
Color.hsla : h:float -> s:float -> l:float -> a:float -> Color.t
Color.of_hex : string -> (Color.t, string) result
Color.lerp : Color.t -> Color.t -> float -> Color.t
Color.categorical : Color.t array     (* 10 distinct colors *)

(* Paint fills *)
type Paint.t = Solid of Color.t
             | Linear_gradient of { x0; y0; x1; y1; stops }
             | Radial_gradient of { cx; cy; r; stops }
             | No_paint

(* Scene primitives *)
Scene.rect   : ?rx -> ?ry -> ?fill -> ?stroke -> x -> y -> w -> h -> unit -> Scene.t
Scene.circle : ?fill -> ?stroke -> cx -> cy -> r -> unit -> Scene.t
Scene.text   : ?font_size -> ?font_family -> ?font_weight -> ?fill -> ?anchor -> ?baseline -> x -> y -> string -> Scene.t
Scene.group  : ?opacity -> ?blend -> ?transforms -> Scene.t list -> Scene.t

(* Path building *)
Path.smooth_curve  : (float * float) list -> Path.segment list   (* Catmull-Rom spline *)
Path.straight_line : (float * float) list -> Path.segment list
Path.closed_area   : (float * float) list -> Path.segment list

(* Data-to-pixel mapping *)
Scale.create : domain:(float * float) -> range:(float * float) -> Scale.t
Scale.apply  : Scale.t -> float -> float
Scale.invert : Scale.t -> float -> float
```

### SVG Renderer (`nopal_svg`)

Pure SVG 1.1 string renderer for `nopal_scene` types. No platform deps — compiles native.

```ocaml
Nopal_svg.render : width:float -> height:float -> Scene.t list -> string
(* Renders a list of scene nodes to a complete SVG document string.
   Emits <defs> for gradients and clip paths. Output includes xmlns and viewBox. *)

(* Low-level formatting module, re-exported for unit testing *)
module Svg_fmt : sig
  type ctx
  val create_ctx          : unit -> ctx
  val color_to_css        : Color.t -> string
  val paint_to_fill_attr  : ctx -> Paint.t -> string
  val stroke_to_attrs     : ctx -> Paint.stroke -> string
  val transform_to_attr   : Transform.t -> string
  val transforms_to_attr  : Transform.t list -> string
  val path_to_d           : Path.segment list -> string
  val blend_to_css        : Scene.blend -> string
  val line_cap_to_string  : Paint.line_cap -> string
  val line_join_to_string : Paint.line_join -> string
  val render_node         : ctx -> Buffer.t -> Scene.t -> unit
  val defs_to_string      : ctx -> string
end
```

Typical usage with charts:

```ocaml
let scene = Bar.scene ~data ~label ~value ~color ~width:400.0 ~height:250.0 () in
let svg_string = Nopal_svg.render ~width:400.0 ~height:250.0 scene
```

### Charts (`nopal_charts`)

Composable interactive charts built on `nopal_draw`:

```ocaml
(* Bar chart — ?domain_window clips data when ?x is also provided *)
Bar.view : data:'a list -> label:('a -> string) -> value:('a -> float)
  -> color:('a -> Color.t) -> ?x:('a -> float) -> width:float -> height:float
  -> ?padding:Padding.t -> ?x_axis:Axis.config -> ?y_axis:Axis.config
  -> ?format_tooltip:('a -> 'msg Element.t) -> ?on_hover:(Hover.t -> 'msg)
  -> ?on_leave:'msg -> ?hover:Hover.t -> ?domain_window:Domain_window.t
  -> unit -> 'msg Element.t

(* Line chart — ?domain_window clips data with buffer=1, rescales Y *)
Line.view : series:'a Line.series list -> x:('a -> float) -> width:float -> height:float
  -> ?padding:Padding.t -> ?x_axis:Axis.config -> ?y_axis:Axis.config
  -> ?format_tooltip:((string * float) list -> 'msg Element.t)
  -> ?on_hover:(Hover.t -> 'msg) -> ?on_leave:'msg -> ?hover:Hover.t
  -> ?domain_window:Domain_window.t
  -> ?on_pointer_down:(Element.pointer_event -> 'msg)
  -> ?on_pointer_up:(Element.pointer_event -> 'msg)
  -> ?on_wheel:(Element.wheel_event -> 'msg)
  -> unit -> 'msg Element.t

(* Area chart — Stacked | Overlapping modes; ?domain_window clips with buffer=1 *)
Area.view : series:'a Area.series list -> x:('a -> float) -> width:float -> height:float
  -> ?mode:Area.mode -> ?padding:Padding.t -> ?x_axis:Axis.config -> ?y_axis:Axis.config
  -> ?format_tooltip:((string * float) list -> 'msg Element.t)
  -> ?on_hover:(Hover.t -> 'msg) -> ?on_leave:'msg -> ?hover:Hover.t
  -> ?domain_window:Domain_window.t -> unit -> 'msg Element.t

(* Pie/donut chart — inner_radius 0.0 = pie, >0.0 = donut *)
Pie.view : data:'a list -> value:('a -> float) -> label:('a -> string)
  -> color:('a -> Color.t) -> width:float -> height:float
  -> ?inner_radius:float -> ?label_threshold:float
  -> ?format_tooltip:('a -> 'msg Element.t) -> ?on_hover:(Hover.t -> 'msg)
  -> ?on_leave:'msg -> ?hover:Hover.t -> unit -> 'msg Element.t

(* Scatter/bubble chart — ?domain_window clips data with buffer=0 *)
Scatter.view : data:'a list -> x:('a -> float) -> y:('a -> float)
  -> ?radius:('a -> float) -> color:('a -> Color.t) -> width:float -> height:float
  -> ?padding:Padding.t -> ?x_axis:Axis.config -> ?y_axis:Axis.config
  -> ?format_tooltip:('a -> 'msg Element.t) -> ?on_hover:(Hover.t -> 'msg)
  -> ?on_leave:'msg -> ?hover:Hover.t -> ?domain_window:Domain_window.t
  -> unit -> 'msg Element.t

(* Sparkline — minimal inline chart *)
Sparkline.view : data:float list -> width:float -> height:float
  -> ?color:Color.t -> ?stroke_width:float -> unit -> 'msg Element.t
```

Chart hover state: `Hover.t = { index: int; series: int; cursor_x: float; cursor_y: float }`

#### Axis Configuration

`Axis.config` is the record the `?x_axis` / `?y_axis` arguments above carry.
Paint and metrics live in a nested `appearance` record on it, so a caller
reaches axis colours through the same argument as `label` and `tick_count`
rather than a parallel one:

```ocaml
type Axis.appearance = {
  line_color : Color.t;         (* axis line stroke; default rgb 0.2 0.2 0.2 *)
  line_width : float;           (* width of the axis line AND of every tick
                                   mark — there is no separate tick width;
                                   default 1.0 *)
  tick_color : Color.t;         (* tick mark stroke; default rgb 0.2 0.2 0.2 *)
  tick_length : float;          (* tick length measured away from the plot
                                   area — below the line on X, left of it on
                                   Y; default 6.0. Ceiling 16.0: the offset
                                   placing the tick labels is private and
                                   fixed at 16.0, so a longer tick runs
                                   through them. Not validated. *)
  tick_label_color : Color.t;   (* per-tick value labels; default Color.black *)
  tick_label_size : float;      (* default 11.0. Ceiling 16.0: the private
                                   tick-label (16.0) and axis-label (32.0)
                                   offsets leave a fixed 16.0 gap, so on an X
                                   axis a larger size overlaps the axis
                                   label. Not validated. *)
  axis_label_color : Color.t;   (* the single caption drawn when config.label
                                   is Some; default Color.black *)
  axis_label_size : float;      (* default 12.0 *)
}

type Axis.config = {
  label : string option;        (* Some => an axis caption is drawn *)
  min : float option;           (* explicit domain override, else nice bounds *)
  max : float option;
  tick_count : int;             (* default 5 *)
  format_tick : float -> string;(* default string_of_float *)
  appearance : Axis.appearance; (* default Axis.default_appearance *)
}

Axis.default_appearance : Axis.appearance
Axis.default_config     : Axis.config
Axis.equal_appearance   : Axis.appearance -> Axis.appearance -> bool
(* Structural equality; float fields compare with Float.equal. There is no
   equal for config, because format_tick is a function. *)
```

The two label colours default to `Color.black` and not to the axis grey —
that is the colour an unfilled text node paints. Omitting `?x_axis` / `?y_axis`
entirely, or passing `Axis.default_config`, renders exactly as the charts did
before appearance was configurable.

Source compatibility is a separate matter from that behavioural one:
`Axis.config` gained a **required** field, so any downstream full-literal
construction or record pattern of `Axis.config` must add `appearance` to keep
compiling — or switch to `{ Axis.default_config with ... }`, which is the
recommended spelling and survives the next field addition.

`Bar` draws its own X axis line and X axis caption instead of calling
`Axis.render_x`, and reads both off `x_axis.appearance`, so a themed colour
applies to a bar chart's X axis too. Its per-bar category labels are not axis
chrome and are not configurable.

```ocaml
(* A themed axis. Spell out the eight-field appearance record in full — it is
   pure paint, and { Axis.default_appearance with ... } inherits colours the
   call site never states. Build config the other way, onto the defaults:
   config is the record the framework extends, so a full literal there turns
   the next added field into a compile error at your call site. Both sizes
   below stay under the 16.0 ceilings noted above. *)
let axis_appearance =
  { Axis.line_color = Color.rgb ~r:0.8 ~g:0.1 ~b:0.1;
    line_width = 3.0;
    tick_color = Color.rgb ~r:0.0 ~g:0.55 ~b:0.55;
    tick_length = 12.0;
    tick_label_color = Color.rgb ~r:0.1 ~g:0.2 ~b:0.6;
    tick_label_size = 15.0;
    axis_label_color = Color.rgb ~r:0.5 ~g:0.0 ~b:0.5;
    axis_label_size = 20.0 }

(* Bar reads x_axis.appearance for the X axis line and caption it draws
   itself, so pass both to theme the whole frame. *)
let x_axis =
  { Axis.default_config with
    label = Some "Quarter"; appearance = axis_appearance }

let y_axis =
  { Axis.default_config with
    label = Some "Revenue"; appearance = axis_appearance }

let chart = Bar.view ~data ~label ~value ~color ~width:400.0 ~height:250.0
              ~x_axis ~y_axis ()
```

#### Scene Functions

Every chart module exposes a `scene` function that returns `Scene.t list` for
pure SVG export or embedding in composite scenes. Scene functions accept the
same data/layout parameters as `view` but omit interaction parameters
(`on_hover`, `on_leave`, `hover`, `format_tooltip`, event handlers).

```ocaml
Bar.scene       : data:'a list -> label:('a -> string) -> value:('a -> float)
  -> color:('a -> Color.t) -> ?x:('a -> float) -> width:float -> height:float
  -> ?padding:Padding.t -> ?x_axis:Axis.config -> ?y_axis:Axis.config
  -> ?domain_window:Domain_window.t -> unit -> Scene.t list

Line.scene      : series:'a Line.series list -> x:('a -> float) -> width:float -> height:float
  -> ?padding:Padding.t -> ?x_axis:Axis.config -> ?y_axis:Axis.config
  -> ?domain_window:Domain_window.t -> unit -> Scene.t list

Area.scene      : series:'a Area.series list -> x:('a -> float) -> width:float -> height:float
  -> ?mode:Area.mode -> ?padding:Padding.t -> ?x_axis:Axis.config -> ?y_axis:Axis.config
  -> ?domain_window:Domain_window.t -> unit -> Scene.t list

Pie.scene       : data:'a list -> value:('a -> float) -> label:('a -> string)
  -> color:('a -> Color.t) -> width:float -> height:float
  -> ?inner_radius:float -> ?label_threshold:float -> unit -> Scene.t list

Scatter.scene   : data:'a list -> x:('a -> float) -> y:('a -> float)
  -> ?radius:('a -> float) -> color:('a -> Color.t) -> width:float -> height:float
  -> ?padding:Padding.t -> ?x_axis:Axis.config -> ?y_axis:Axis.config
  -> ?domain_window:Domain_window.t -> unit -> Scene.t list

Heat_map.scene  : data:'a list -> row:('a -> int) -> col:('a -> int)
  -> value:('a -> float) -> row_count:int -> col_count:int
  -> ?row_labels:string list -> ?col_labels:string list
  -> scale:Color_scale.t -> width:float -> height:float
  -> ?padding:Padding.t -> unit -> Scene.t list

Sparkline.scene : data:float list -> width:float -> height:float
  -> ?color:Color.t -> ?stroke_width:float -> unit -> Scene.t list

Trading.Candlestick.scene : data:'a list -> x:('a -> float)
  -> open_:('a -> float) -> high:('a -> float) -> low:('a -> float) -> close:('a -> float)
  -> width:float -> height:float -> ?padding:Padding.t
  -> ?bullish_color:Color.t -> ?bearish_color:Color.t
  -> ?x_axis:Axis.config -> ?y_axis:Axis.config
  -> ?domain_window:Domain_window.t -> unit -> Scene.t list

Trading.Drawdown.scene : data:'a list -> x:('a -> float) -> y:('a -> float)
  -> width:float -> height:float -> ?padding:Padding.t
  -> ?fill_color:Color.t -> ?x_axis:Axis.config -> ?y_axis:Axis.config
  -> ?domain_window:Domain_window.t -> unit -> Scene.t list
```

#### Heat Map

Renders a 2D grid of colored cells using `Color_scale`. Uses the accessor
pattern for API consistency with other chart types:

```ocaml
Heat_map.view : data:'a list -> row:('a -> int) -> col:('a -> int)
  -> value:('a -> float) -> row_count:int -> col_count:int
  -> ?row_labels:string list -> ?col_labels:string list
  -> scale:Color_scale.t -> width:float -> height:float
  -> ?padding:Padding.t
  -> ?format_tooltip:('a -> 'msg Element.t)
  -> ?on_hover:(Hover.t -> 'msg) -> ?on_leave:'msg -> ?hover:Hover.t
  -> unit -> 'msg Element.t
```

#### Trading Namespace

Convenient grouping of trading-specific chart types:

```ocaml
module Trading : sig
  module Candlestick = Trading_candlestick
  module Drawdown = Trading_drawdown
end
```

**Candlestick chart** — OHLC candles with wicks:

```ocaml
Trading.Candlestick.view : data:'a list -> x:('a -> float)
  -> open_:('a -> float) -> high:('a -> float) -> low:('a -> float) -> close:('a -> float)
  -> width:float -> height:float -> ?padding:Padding.t
  -> ?bullish_color:Color.t -> ?bearish_color:Color.t
  -> ?x_axis:Axis.config -> ?y_axis:Axis.config
  -> ?format_tooltip:(int -> float -> float -> float -> float -> 'msg Element.t)
  -> ?on_hover:(Hover.t -> 'msg) -> ?on_leave:'msg -> ?hover:Hover.t
  -> ?domain_window:Domain_window.t -> unit -> 'msg Element.t
(* Bullish (close > open) and bearish candles use distinct colors.
   format_tooltip receives index and OHLC values. Clips via Viewport with buffer=0. *)
```

**Drawdown chart** — inverted area from 0% baseline downward:

```ocaml
Trading.Drawdown.view : data:'a list -> x:('a -> float) -> y:('a -> float)
  -> width:float -> height:float -> ?padding:Padding.t
  -> ?fill_color:Color.t -> ?x_axis:Axis.config -> ?y_axis:Axis.config
  -> ?format_tooltip:(int -> float -> 'msg Element.t)
  -> ?on_hover:(Hover.t -> 'msg) -> ?on_leave:'msg -> ?hover:Hover.t
  -> ?domain_window:Domain_window.t -> unit -> 'msg Element.t
(* Y values should be <= 0.0 (drawdown percentages). Y domain: [min_drawdown, 0.0].
   fill_color defaults to semi-transparent red. Clips via Viewport with buffer=1. *)
```

#### Color Scale

Maps data values to colors via interpolation:

```ocaml
Color_scale.sequential : low:Color.t -> high:Color.t -> Color_scale.t
Color_scale.diverging : low:Color.t -> mid:Color.t -> high:Color.t
  -> ?midpoint:float -> unit -> Color_scale.t
Color_scale.apply : Color_scale.t -> min:float -> max:float -> float -> Color.t
(* Values outside [min, max] are clamped. Diverging midpoint defaults to 0.0. *)
```

#### Domain Window

Visible X-axis range for pan/zoom:

```ocaml
type Domain_window.t = { x_min : float; x_max : float }

Domain_window.create : x_min:float -> x_max:float -> Domain_window.t
Domain_window.equal  : Domain_window.t -> Domain_window.t -> bool
Domain_window.width  : Domain_window.t -> float
Domain_window.pan    : Domain_window.t -> delta:float -> Domain_window.t
Domain_window.zoom   : Domain_window.t -> center:float -> factor:float -> Domain_window.t
(* zoom factor < 1.0 zooms in, > 1.0 zooms out. Center maintains relative position. *)

Domain_window.clamp  : data_min:float -> data_max:float -> Domain_window.t -> Domain_window.t
(* IMPORTANT: pan/zoom do NOT clamp. Always pipe through clamp after every
   pan/zoom to prevent the window from sliding past the data range:
     Domain_window.pan dw ~delta |> Domain_window.clamp ~data_min:0.0 ~data_max:999.0
   Without clamp, the chart will go blank when the user drags past the data. *)
```

Typical pan/zoom update pattern (drag-to-pan + wheel-to-zoom + button zoom):

```ocaml
(* In your model: domain_window : Domain_window.t; drag_start_x : float option *)
let clamp_dw dw = Domain_window.clamp ~data_min:0.0 ~data_max:999.0 dw

(* Drag to pan *)
| PointerDown x -> ({ model with drag_start_x = Some x }, Cmd.none)
| PointerMove x ->
    (match model.drag_start_x with
     | None -> (model, Cmd.none)
     | Some last_x ->
         let scale = Domain_window.width model.domain_window /. chart_w in
         let delta = -.(( x -. last_x) *. scale) in
         let dw = Domain_window.pan model.domain_window ~delta |> clamp_dw in
         ({ model with domain_window = dw; drag_start_x = Some x }, Cmd.none))
| PointerUp | PointerLeave -> ({ model with drag_start_x = None }, Cmd.none)

(* Wheel to zoom — on_wheel:(fun we -> WheelZoom we) *)
| WheelZoom we ->
    let frac = we.x /. chart_w in
    let center = dw.x_min +. (frac *. Domain_window.width dw) in
    let factor = if we.delta_y > 0.0 then 1.2 else 1.0 /. 1.2 in
    let dw' = Domain_window.zoom dw ~center ~factor |> clamp_dw in
    ({ model with domain_window = dw' }, Cmd.none)

(* Button zoom — zooms around center *)
| ZoomIn ->
    let center = (dw.x_min +. dw.x_max) /. 2.0 in
    let dw' = Domain_window.zoom dw ~center ~factor:0.5 |> clamp_dw in
    ({ model with domain_window = dw' }, Cmd.none)
```

#### Chart Pane

Multi-pane synchronized layout:

```ocaml
type 'msg Chart_pane.pane = {
  height_ratio : float;
  chart : Domain_window.t -> width:float -> height:float -> 'msg Element.t;
  y_axis : Axis.config option;
}

Chart_pane.pane : height_ratio:float -> ?y_axis:Axis.config
  -> (Domain_window.t -> width:float -> height:float -> 'msg Element.t)
  -> 'msg Chart_pane.pane
(* NOTE: pane's y_axis is currently inert — the record stores it and nothing in
   Chart_pane reads it, so it neither draws nor themes an axis. Configure the
   axis on the chart the pane wraps instead. *)

Chart_pane.view : panes:'msg Chart_pane.pane list -> domain_window:Domain_window.t
  -> width:float -> height:float
  -> ?on_pointer_down:(Element.pointer_event -> 'msg)
  -> ?on_pointer_move:(Element.pointer_event -> 'msg)
  -> ?on_pointer_up:(Element.pointer_event -> 'msg)
  -> ?on_pointer_leave:'msg
  -> ?on_wheel:(Element.wheel_event -> 'msg)
  -> unit -> 'msg Element.t
(* Panes are vertically stacked; height_ratios normalized to sum to 1.0.
   Each pane's chart function receives the shared domain_window plus the
   computed pixel width and height. Raw pointer/wheel events are forwarded
   so the caller can implement pan/zoom in their update function. *)
```

#### Viewport

Clips data to visible domain window:

```ocaml
Viewport.clip : x:('a -> float) -> data:'a list -> window:Domain_window.t
  -> buffer:int -> 'a list
Viewport.clip_sorted : x:('a -> float) -> data:'a array -> window:Domain_window.t
  -> buffer:int -> 'a array
(* buffer=1 for line/area (path continuity), buffer=0 for bar/scatter.
   clip_sorted uses binary search — O(log n) vs O(n). *)
```

#### Downsample (LTTB)

Reduces large datasets while preserving visual shape:

```ocaml
Downsample.lttb : x:('a -> float) -> y:('a -> float) -> data:'a array
  -> target:int -> 'a array
Downsample.should_downsample : data_length:int -> pixel_width:float -> bool
Downsample.target_for_width  : pixel_width:float -> int
(* Threshold: 3x pixels. Target: 2x pixels. First/last points always preserved. *)
```

Find nearest data point for crosshair/tooltip:
